official.deadline_central_display: 6 October 2026 (national deadline for the 2027-2028 cycle; now closed)
official.deadline_note: The 2027-2028 competition is closed. The 2028-2029 award cycle application launches Spring 2027 and its national deadline is not yet published. Institutional campus deadlines are typically 4-6 weeks earlier than the national October deadline; recommendation letters and all components were due by the national deadline.
official.application_cycle: 2028-2029 award cycle - application launching Spring 2027 (2027-2028 competition closed 6 October 2026)
official.status_note: The official site states the application for the 2027-2028 Competition is now closed and the 2028-2029 Award Cycle application is launching Spring 2027; semi-finalist notification for 2027-2028 is expected by end of January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: 'Based on award and country, some grants may also include ... Full or partial tuition' - tuition is not covered on every award, so the graduate-degree award descriptions and country summaries must be checked.
benefits: A stipend broadly based on the cost of living in the host country, usable for room, board, and incidental costs during the grant period
24/7 support line for urgent and non-urgent situations
12 months of non-competitive eligibility (NCE) hiring status within the federal government
Round-trip transportation to the host country and pre-departure and/or in-country orientations (Post countries)
Based on award and country: book and research allowances, mid-term enrichment activities, full or partial tuition, and language study programs
eligibility: Citizens or nationals of the United States at the time of the application deadline; permanent residents are not eligible

A conferred bachelor's degree or equivalent before the start of the grant period (in the creative and performing arts, four years of professional training and/or experience meets the basic eligibility requirement)
No doctoral degree (Ph.D.) held by the national application deadline; applicants may hold a J.D.
No residence abroad for five or more years in the six-year period preceding the national application deadline
Applicants must meet the language requirements of the award to which they are applying
Preference for applicants who have not previously held a Fulbright grant and whose higher education was undertaken primarily at educational institutions in the United States
requirements: Application submitted through the Fulbright online application system by the campus (institutional) or national deadline
Three recommendation letters, submitted confidentially by the recommenders through the online system
Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions from which degrees were received
For Study/Research awards: a proposed host-country affiliation listed, with a signed affiliation letter where the award requires one at the time of application
Language Self-Evaluation plus a Foreign Language Evaluation Form by a professional language teacher where the award requires language proficiency
documents: Three recommendation letters (confidential, uploaded by the recommenders, on institutional letterhead, in English or with English translation)
Academic transcripts from every degree-granting institution (unofficial registrar-produced transcripts accepted; portal screenshots rejected)
Letter of affiliation from the host-country institution or sponsoring entity, where required at application (institutional letterhead, signed, in English or translated)
Foreign Language Evaluation Form, where required by the award
Short answers: Flexibility & Adaptability, Community Engagement, and Impact of Fulbright Award
Biographical data, project title (90 characters) and abstract (1,750 characters), plus supplementary materials for creative and performing arts applicants
selection_criteria: Project Proposal & Grant Purpose: quality and feasibility of the proposal as described in the Statement of Grant Purpose, aligned with the Award Description parameters
Qualifications: academic and/or professional record, relevant training, accomplishments, extracurricular activities, and language preparation
Contribution to the Fulbright Mission, including preference factors set by the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board and the Fulbright Commissions/Foundations
Ability of the supervising agencies abroad to arrange or confirm supervision and facilitate research clearance where necessary
Country-specific requirements: in some countries advanced-degree candidates are preferred and certain fields of study are not recommended
coverage: Room, board, and incidental costs through a stipend broadly based on the cost of living in the host country
Round-trip transportation to the host country (Post countries)
Full or partial tuition, book and research allowances, mid-term enrichment activities, and language study programs, based on award and country
application_method: Confirm eligibility and determine applicant type: through a U.S. institution or At-Large
Contact the campus Fulbright Program Adviser and confirm the campus deadline, typically 4-6 weeks before the national October deadline
Complete the Fulbright online application, register recommenders and any language evaluator, and mark the application 'Ready for Campus Review' if applying through an institution
Attend the campus interview, revise with feedback after the FPA unlocks the application, then personally submit before the National Deadline - submissions are final and cannot be unsubmitted
official.application_route: Apply online through the Fulbright online application system, either through your campus Fulbright Program Adviser (institutional route with campus interview) or as an At-Large candidate, and submit before the national October deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time; grant dates traditionally correspond to the host country's academic calendar, with exceptions to stated start dates possible for full-time research projects
official.citizenship_residency: Open to U.S. citizens or nationals only; permanent residents are not eligible, and anyone who has resided abroad for five or more years in the six-year period preceding the national application deadline is ineligible.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international students - only U.S. citizens and nationals. Non-U.S. citizens apply for Fulbright awards to the United States through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in their home country (e.g., the Fulbright Foreign Student Program).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open in all academic disciplines and the creative and performing arts, but some countries do not recommend certain fields of study, some prefer advanced-degree candidates, and named awards exist for specific fields - check the country Award Description before applying.
official.research_requirement: Study/Research applicants design their own independent study or research project (or a graduate degree program where the country allows) and must list a proposed host-country affiliation; research involving human or animal subjects should be vetted by the home institution's IRB, and grantees may need host-country research clearance.
official.duration: Typically one academic year or more, as specified in the country Award Description; for the 2027-2028 academic year grants had to begin no later than June 1, 2028.
official.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program, a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by IIE, funds American citizens to study, conduct research, or teach English abroad. It offers Study/Research awards in approximately 140 countries, English Teaching Assistant awards, the Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program, and Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health, with over 1,800 awards annually.
official.program_type: Government-funded international exchange grant (U.S. Department of State program administered by IIE)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL score is published. Applicants must meet the language requirements of the award to which they are applying and demonstrate sufficient competency to complete the project and adjust to life in the host country. Where a language is required, the Language Self-Evaluation and a Foreign Language Evaluation Form completed by a professional language teacher are mandatory; for countries where English is a national language, no foreign language forms are needed unless the project requires a foreign language.

verification.notes: Deadline, benefits, eligibility, documents, and selection criteria were confirmed directly on the official us.fulbrightonline.org pages on 2026-10-10. The official Award Benefits page publishes no stipend figure, stating only that the stipend is broadly based on the cost of living in the host country, so amount, currency, and period are recorded as null rather than guessed.

applicant_utility.summary: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program funds U.S. citizens to study, research, or teach English abroad, paying a host-country cost-of-living stipend plus accident and sickness health benefits and round-trip airfare, with full or partial tuition included only on some awards and countries. The 2027-2028 round closed on 6 October 2026; the next application window opens in Spring 2027 for the 2028-2029 cycle. Your campus Fulbright Program Adviser is the first call, because institutional applicants must clear a campus interview and personally submit their locked application before the national deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizens without a PhD who want a self-designed year of research, graduate study, or English teaching abroad and can invest months in securing a host-country affiliation and three confidential recommendations.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your Fulbright Program Adviser immediately to confirm the campus deadline, which typically falls 4-6 weeks before the national October deadline
Start securing a host-country affiliation months ahead and obtain the signed letterhead affiliation letter early where the award requires one at application - late letters are not accepted
Line up three recommenders and give them 4-5 weeks, since letters upload confidentially through the system and you cannot submit them yourself
Order registrar-produced transcripts (unofficial is fine, portal screenshots are not) from every institution that granted you a degree
Check the award's language requirements and register a professional language evaluator early if a Foreign Language Evaluation is required
Check the duplicative-funding rule: Fulbright benefits may be reduced if another grant covers the same costs
common_rejection_risks: Missing the campus deadline or assuming your Fulbright Program Adviser submits for you - submissions are final and only the applicant can submit

Applying to a country award whose requirements you fail (host-country residency limits, restricted fields, affiliation type), which is screened out in the October technical review before any committee reads it
No affiliation letter at the deadline for an award that requires one, or an affiliate that does not meet the country's requirements
Hard eligibility failures: holding a PhD by the deadline, having lived abroad five or more of the last six years, or being a permanent resident rather than a citizen
An infeasible or generic Statement of Grant Purpose - reviewers explicitly judge feasibility, host-country fit, and concrete community engagement plans
Formatting traps: URLs or personal contact details in essays can render the application ineligible, and excessive paragraph breaks can cut text off in the PDF proof
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend covers room, board and incidental costs only; visa fees, dependent costs, and tuition on awards without full tuition coverage remain the grantee's responsibility, Fulbright benefits may be reduced if duplicated by another grant, and commission-country benefits may differ significantly.
document_audit: Transcripts must be registrar-produced, show your name and institution, and list course dates, titles, credits and grades chronologically - portal screenshots and pasted Word files are rejected

The affiliation letter must be on institutional letterhead, signed, in English or translated by you, and never written by a relative; email correspondence is not accepted and only the affiliation letter belongs in that upload field
Recommendation letters are confidential - you cannot upload them for recommenders, and any resubmission request must be made through the system before the national deadline
Essays must contain no URLs or personal contact details, and the Review & Submit PDF proof must be checked for responses cut off by paragraph breaks
alerts: The 2027-2028 competition is closed - the 2028-2029 application only launches in Spring 2027, so treat any October 2026 deadline claims as stale
Campus deadlines run 4-6 weeks ahead of the national deadline, and marking the application 'Ready for Campus Review' locks it until the FPA unlocks it after the interview
Grant start dates follow the host country's academic calendar - for 2027-2028 grants had to begin no later than June 1, 2028
Recent Fulbright participants (2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 cohorts) remain eligible but are at a competitive disadvantage
You cannot apply to the Fulbright Student and Scholar programs in the same cycle, or for more than one Student grant in one cycle
Final selections roll out March through June and cannot be predicted; host-country review may include interviews and extra document requests
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register recommenders and any language evaluator early, complete the online application and mark it ready for campus review, clear the campus interview and revisions, then personally submit before the national deadline - no late items and no unsubmitting.
